title: Sanitize the import asset name before it becomes a C++ identifier
body:
## Summary
The Import Automation asset name is pasted verbatim into generated C++ class names, so any name with a space or punctuation produces code that cannot compile.

## Description
The Asset Name field in src/components/modules/visual-gen/import-automation/ImportAutomationView.tsx feeds generateImportScript and generateDataAsset. src/lib/visual-gen/ue5-import-templates.ts:96 emits `class U${config.assetName}Importer` and :154 emits `class U${config.assetName}Data`, and :89 and :148 use it in a generated.h include. Nothing validates or normalizes it. Fixed means a derived identifier (or a refusal shown beside the field) for the two class names and the includes, while the display string stays as typed.

## Flow
- type `Stone Wall` into Asset Name
- the preview shows `class UStone WallImporter`
- the operator copies code UHT and the compiler reject

## Expected impact
Operators stop copying generated C++ that cannot compile. Could break: anything pinning the emitted text for a name that needs no change must stay byte-identical.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - generated C++ is compilable for any typed name
Before: 2 class declarations and 2 includes interpolate the raw name; `Stone Wall` yields an invalid identifier by reading the template
After: predicted 0 invalid identifiers for names with spaces or punctuation
Method: simulation - read of the template with three names (MyAsset, Stone Wall, 3dRock); the fix is in lib/visual-gen, outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/lib/visual-gen/ue5-import-templates.ts:89 #include "${config.assetName}Importer.generated.h"
src/lib/visual-gen/ue5-import-templates.ts:96 class U${config.assetName}Importer : public UEditorUtilityWidget
src/lib/visual-gen/ue5-import-templates.ts:148 #include "${config.assetName}Data.generated.h"
src/lib/visual-gen/ue5-import-templates.ts:154 class U${config.assetName}Data : public UPrimaryDataAsset
instrument: Vitest over generateImportScript and generateDataAsset with names containing spaces, punctuation and a leading digit, asserting every `class U...` token matches a C++ identifier pattern and that MyAsset output is unchanged

title: Block out in Blender can be re-run into a second collection after success
body:
## Summary
After a confirmed blockout the button stays enabled, and each further click builds another full copy of the proxies in a new collection.

## Description
src/components/modules/visual-gen/scene-composer/SceneDressPanel.tsx:77 computes canBuild without excluding status `built`, and useSceneDressStore.ts:104 only blocks busy states. src/lib/blender-mcp/scripts/composition-blockout.ts:63 always calls bpy.data.collections.new, which Blender uniquifies, so repeated clicks accumulate collections. The same applies after `unconfirmed`, where the first build may have landed. Fixed means re-running is a stated choice: the label says it adds another copy, or a built plan requires an explicit rebuild.

## Flow
- Decompose an image and click Block out; Blender confirms N proxies
- click Block out again
- the scene now holds 2N proxies in two collections, and the status line still reports N

## Expected impact
Operators stop accumulating duplicate blockouts by accident. Could break: a deliberate variant workflow that relies on additive builds, which is why the behaviour needs choosing rather than removing.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a repeated click cannot silently duplicate the blockout
Before: 1 of 1 terminal success states leaves the build button enabled (reading canBuild); script always creates a new collection
After: predicted 0 unannounced duplicate builds
Method: simulation - walked built, unconfirmed and build-failed through canBuild; a real duplicate needs a live Blender, which this round may not run
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/components/modules/visual-gen/scene-composer/SceneDressPanel.tsx:77 const canBuild = connected && placed > 0 && !busy && status !== 'failed' && status !== 'empty';
src/lib/blender-mcp/scripts/composition-blockout.ts:63 coll = bpy.data.collections.new("${BLOCKOUT_COLLECTION}")
instrument: Component test of SceneDressPanel in status built asserting the build control is disabled or relabelled as an additional copy, plus a store test counting dispatches

title: Refuse oversized reference images before the paid scene decompose
body:
## Summary
Dress from image reads any picked file into a data URL and posts it to a paid vision route, with no size limit on either side.

## Description
src/components/modules/visual-gen/scene-composer/SceneDressPanel.tsx:59-72 passes the file straight to readAsDataURL with no file.size check. useSceneDressStore.ts:85-89 stringifies it into the request. src/app/api/visual-gen/scene-decompose/route.ts:86-88 only checks that the field exists and parses. A grep of src/lib/visual-gen/input-gate.ts for size or MAX_ finds no limit. Fixed means one stated byte limit, refused beside the picker before any read, and enforced again on the route.

## Flow
- pick a very large image
- the browser base64-encodes all of it into store state
- Decompose posts it, and the failure arrives only as a provider or body-size error after the attempt

## Expected impact
Operators get an immediate, named refusal instead of a stalled tab or an opaque provider failure. Could break: a legitimately large reference if the limit is set too low.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - oversized input is refused before work is done
Before: 0 size checks across panel, store and route (read of all three, grep of input-gate)
After: predicted 1 client refusal and 1 route refusal at one shared constant
Method: simulation - traced the path; the route is outside this round's paths and the provider's real limit needs a paid call to establish
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: Component test feeding a File over the limit and asserting no FileReader read and a visible refusal, plus a route test asserting 413 with no vision call (mocked)
